claims.claim: Opens with letters from Robert Walton writing from St. Petersburgh to his sister Mrs. Saville
claims.evidence: 'To Mrs. Saville, England. St. Petersburgh, Dec. 11th'; 'my dear sister'

claims.claim: Walton is an English explorer setting out toward the North Pole
claims.evidence: 'a voyage of discovery towards the northern pole'

claims.claim: His ship meets Victor Frankenstein on the ice
claims.evidence: sledge drifted on a fragment of ice; a European addresses him in English
Chapter 1: 'I am by birth a Genevese'

claims.claim: Victor is a Genevese student at Ingolstadt
claims.evidence: 'I am by birth a Genevese'; 'student at the university of Ingolstadt'

claims.claim: Victor makes a living creature, is horrified and flees
The creature learns language watching the De Lacey family, is driven away
claims.evidence: 'I learned and applied the words, fire, milk, bread'; 'enraged Felix tearing me from his father's feet'

claims.claim: The creature kills William; Justine is condemned
He demands a female companion; Victor begins, then destroys her
claims.evidence: 'You must create a female for me'; 'remains of the half-finished creature, whom I had destroyed'

claims.claim: Creature kills Elizabeth on the wedding night
claims.evidence: 'I shall be with you on your wedding-night'; Elizabeth's murder
'he died in my arms' after tidings

claims.claim: Victor pursues the creature north, dies aboard Walton's ship
claims.evidence: 'the cabin where lay the remains of my ill-fated friend'

claims.claim: Creature mourns, vows to burn himself on a funeral pile, lost on the ice
claims.evidence: 'I shall collect my funeral pile'; 'borne away by the waves and lost in darkness'

claims.claim: Walton is an English sea captain who records Victor's tale
claims.evidence: 'Here is our captain'; letters to sister

claims.claim: Elizabeth Lavenza: Victor's adopted cousin, raised in his family, his bride
claims.evidence: 'Elizabeth Lavenza became the inmate of my parents' house'; 'familiarly by the name of cousin'

claims.claim: Henry Clerval: Victor's loyal childhood friend
claims.evidence: 'Henry Clerval was the son of a merchant of Geneva' (boyhood companion)

claims.claim: Justine Moritz: servant in the Frankenstein household
claims.evidence: 'Justine, thus received in our family'; servant
